How Does Job Loss Affect Our Community?
How Does Job Loss Affect Our Community?
Work

Careers
|
Government Jobs
By Steve Milano Updated June 14, 2021
Reading about job losses can be an abstract experience if you’re learning about losses tied to issues like national unemployment figures. You might understand that the federal government, the stock market and big businesses will react in certain ways, but not about what job losses mean to your city or town.
Understanding how a rise in unemployment can affect you and your community will help you better prepare for consequences and help you protect your job, your personal finances and your business, if you own one.
Local Businesses Might Close
When locals are out of work, they won’t have the same amount of money to spend on dining out, buying clothes, going to the movies or making other discretionary purchases. Depending on how many people in a community are unemployed and how long the downturn lasts, some local businesses might not survive.
If you have a small business in an area facing high unemployment, start running numbers to see how long you can survive. You might be able to start operating at break-even just to pay your bills until things get better. You might not be able to walk away and shut down because you still have carrying costs (long-term leases, insurance, security, property taxes and other obligations). In this case, operating at a $2,000 monthly loss is better than closing and paying $3,000 in monthly carrying costs.
Filing for Chapter 7 bankruptcy protection allows you to continue to operate under a court-approved operating plan so you can reduce your expenses, explains legal website NOLO. You can also file for Chapter 7 protection as an individual.
Salaries, Wages, Benefits Might Decrease
When people are unemployed and face losing their home, savings and retirement money, they are often willing to work for less. The more labor supply in your community, the lower worker pay often drops. Even if you’re employed, if the company you work for starts struggling, it might ask employees to take a pay cut or start cutting staff.
In addition to pay cuts, workers might start losing benefits, such as health insurance or a retirement account contribution. While some employees might be willing to work for benefits rather than be completely unemployed, other workers might offer to give up their benefits so they can continue to earn money to pay their rent, utilities and grocery bills.
Your Retirement Might be Delayed
If you find yourself in a situation where your company cuts your wages or benefits, that might significantly decrease your retirement contributions. If you had planned on retiring at a certain age, this might set you back a year or more. If you actively contribute to one or more retirement accounts, such as an employer 401(k) plan and a personal IRA, talk to a financial advisor to see if you need to be more aggressive with your investments, look at new options or simply ride out the downturn the best you can.
Don’t take money out of your retirement account without consulting a tax advisor. Depending on what type of account you’re raiding, you might face stiff financial penalties for withdrawing funds early from a retirement account.
If your home value is a key part of your retirement planning timetable, remember that significant local unemployment can lead to more foreclosures, reducing housing prices in the area.
There’s More Competition for Work
One of the reasons pay and benefits go down is because more people are available to work and businesses don’t have to offer higher pay and benefits to attract workers. If you’re already employed, this might not be a problem for you. If you’re looking for work, you might need to step up your job search skills because you’ll have more competition.
Get help with your resume and updating your LinkedIn page. If you have time, improve your job skills, either by volunteering at a charity to assist a manager or by taking community college classes.
Your Workload Might Increase
If your company has to lay off employees to keep its doors open, it might need to shift work onto the staff they’re able to keep. This can be as simple as restaurant servers needing to handle more tables each shift. It might mean that marketing or HR staff at a small business might need to start doing sales database entry or answering customer calls.
State and Local Taxes Might Decrease
When local businesses sell less, they generate fewer sales taxes. State and local governments use sales taxes to pay for a variety of public benefits. If you see a serious economic downturn coming to your area, research where your community’s sales taxes go and make plans to be able to manage any cuts governments make to those services.
Charities Start Feeling Pressure
When job losses hit a community hard enough, food banks, soup kitchens, homeless shelters and other charities that provide assistance might face funding shortfalls. In some cases, they won’t be able to provide the important services they offer to the unemployed or working poor.
Even if these charities see new donations coming in from community members and businesses, that means other charities might suffer. For example, when people and businesses start donating money to food banks and soup kitchens, that’s money they can’t donate to youth sports leagues, schools, hospitals and religious organizations.
If you have skills you can donate to charities during times like these, you can help them improve their operations and/or reduce their expenses. You can also improve your job-hunting situation while you’re out of work if you can show an employer you haven’t been idle. Re-doing a charity’s website or helping them update their bookkeeping system is a way to keep project work on your resume, rather than a gap, points out Knew Money.
Social Pressures Mount
When a community has a lack of jobs and a high unemployment rate, it can see an uptick in substance abuse, depression and other psychological and sociological problems that are common effects of losing a job. This can cause increased pressure on charities that deal with these situations, overwhelm hospitals and lead to higher crime. A local rise in unemployment can even cause children to score lower on school exams, according to researchers at Duke University’s Sanford School of Public Policy.
Assume the Worst
Don’t wait until you lose your job to start cutting back your spending, shoring up your savings, updating your resume and improving your job skills. The more prepared you are for possible unemployment, the better your chances are for surviving a local spike in unemployment. If you think your company is likely to be affected by a local rise in unemployment, you might discreetly start searching for a new job with a company you feel is more likely to survive a recession.

Unemployment means being out of job or a situation where the individual is wiling to work but has none.
This article brings and discusses the main issues/effects of the unemployment on our society and economy.
How does unemployment affect the economy?
Some of the well-known effects of unemployment on the economy are:
Unemployment financial costs
The government and the nation suffer. In many countries the government has to pay the unemployed some benefits. The greater the number of the unemployed or the longer they are without work the more money the government has to shell out.
Therefore, the nation not only has to deal with the lost income and decreased production but also with additional cost.
Spending power
The spending power of an unemployed person and his/her family decreases drastically and they would rather save than spend their money, which in turn affects the economy adversely.
Reduced spending power of the employed
Increased taxes and the insecurity about their own work may affect the spending power of the working people as well and they too may start to spend less than before thus affecting the economy and also the society in a negative manner.
Recession
With the increase rates of unemployment other economy factors are significantly affected, such as: the income per person, health costs, quality of health-care, standard of leaving and poverty.
All these affect not just the economy but the entire systems and the society in general. Here are some aspects of the impact of unemployment on our society:
The effect of unemployment on our society
Unemployment affects not just the person himself but also his/her family and in the long run the society where he lives.
Unemployment brings with it despair, unhappiness and anguish. It forces people to live their lives in a way they do not wish to – The life expectancy is negatively affected.
Life expectancy is the ease by which people living in a time/place are able to satisfy their needs/wants. Here are the main aspects:
Mental health: Mental health problems like: Law self-confidence, feeling unworthy, depression and hopelessness. With the lost income and the frustration involved in it, the recently unemployed may develop negative attitudes toward common things in life and may feel that all sense of purpose is lost. Frequent emotions could be – low self-esteem, inadequateness and feeling dejected and hopeless.
Health diseases: The unemployment overall tension can increase dramatically general health issues of individuals.
Tension at home: Quarrels and arguments at home front which may lead to tension and increased numbers of divorces etc.
Political issues: Loss of trust in administration and the government which may lead to political instability
Tension over taxes rise: Unemployment also brings up discontent and frustration amongst the tax paying citizens. In order to meet the demands of the unemployment fund the government many a times may have to increase the taxes thus giving way to restlessness amongst the tax paying citizens.
Insecurity amongst employees: The prevailing unemployment and the plight of the unemployed people and their families may create fear and insecurity even in the currently employed people.
Crime and violence: Increase in the rate of crime.
Suicide cases: Increase in the rate of suicide attempts and actual suicides as well.
Social outing: Unemployment may bring a decrease in social outings and interactions with other people, including friends.
Stigma: Unemployment brings with more than just ‘no work’. It also brings with it the disgrace that the person has to bear. Nobody likes to be termed as unemployed.
Standard of leaving: In times of unemployment the competition for jobs and the negotiation power of the individual decreases and thus also the living standard of people with the salaries packages and income reduced.
Employment gaps: To further complicate the situation the longer the individual is out of job the more difficult it becomes to find one. Employers find employment gasps as a negative aspect. No one wants to hire a person who has been out of work for some time even when there’s no fault of the individual per say.
Lose of skills’ usage: The unemployed is not able to put his/her skills to use. And in a situation where it goes on for too long the person may have to lose some of his/her skills.
